/- ===== Catalog/Pythagorean/FourierPoissonConverse.lean ===== -/

/-
# The converse of Poisson summation: Poisson summation *characterises* subgroups

`Catalog.Pythagorean.FourierSubgroupDuality` proves the "if" direction of finite Poisson
summation: for a subgroup `H ≤ G` of a finite abelian group,

  `|G| * ∑_{x ∈ H} f x = |H| * ∑_{ψ ∈ H^⊥} f̂ ψ`   for every `f : G → ℂ`.

This file settles the **converse**, which was left open there.  For an arbitrary finset
`S ⊆ G` one may still form the annihilator `S^⊥ = {ψ : ψ|_S = 1}` and ask whether the
identity

  `|G| * ∑_{x ∈ S} f x = |S| * ∑_{ψ ∈ S^⊥} f̂ ψ`                                (P_S)

can hold.  Main results:

* `FourierFA.subgroup_of_poissonDelta` : **strong converse / one-test-function rigidity.**
  If (P_S) holds for the *single* Dirac delta `δ_{y₀}` at one point `y₀ ∈ S`, then `S` is
  already the underlying finset of the subgroup generated by `S`.
* `FourierFA.poissonSet_iff_subgroup` : for nonempty `S`, (P_S) holds for all `f` iff `S` is
  a subgroup.
* `FourierFA.poissonSet_iff` : the complete classification, with no hypothesis on `S`:
  (P_S) holds iff `S = ∅` or `S` is a subgroup.  The empty set is a genuine exceptional
  solution (`FourierFA.poissonSet_empty`), so the nonemptiness hypothesis above is sharp.
* `FourierFA.poissonSet_iff_zero_mem_and_sub_mem` : a purely combinatorial form of the
  classification (`0 ∈ S` and `S` is closed under subtraction).
* `FourierFA.poisson_defect_formula` : an exact formula for the *defect* of (P_S), showing
  that it measures precisely the failure of `S` to fill out the subgroup `⟨S⟩` it generates.
* `FourierFA.poisson_gap` : **quantitative rigidity / no near-Poisson sets.** If `S` is
  nonempty and not a subgroup, some Dirac delta witnesses a defect of modulus at least
  `|⟨S⟩| - |S| ≥ 1`; there is no approximate version of the phenomenon.
* `FourierFA.card_closure_mul_card_annihF` : `|⟨S⟩| * |S^⊥| = |G|` for every finset `S`.

Everything is deduced from the catalog's `FourierFA.poisson_summation`, applied to the
subgroup generated by `S`; no Pontryagin duality input beyond what the catalog already has
is needed.
-/

import Mathlib
import Pythagorean.FourierSubgroupDuality

open Finset Fintype ComplexConjugate
open scoped Classical

namespace FourierFA

variable {G : Type*} [AddCommGroup G] [Fintype G] [DecidableEq G]

/-! ## Annihilator of an arbitrary finset, and the subgroup it generates -/

/-- The annihilator `S^⊥ = {ψ : ∀ x ∈ S, ψ x = 1}` of an arbitrary finset `S ⊆ G`. -/
noncomputable def annihF (S : Finset G) : Finset (AddChar G ℂ) :=
  Finset.univ.filter (fun ψ : AddChar G ℂ => ∀ x ∈ S, ψ x = 1)

/-- The subgroup of `G` generated by a finset `S`. -/
noncomputable def closureS (S : Finset G) : AddSubgroup G := AddSubgroup.closure (S : Set G)

/-- The underlying finset of the subgroup generated by `S`. -/
noncomputable def closureF (S : Finset G) : Finset G := subFinset (closureS S)

@[simp] lemma mem_annihF {S : Finset G} {ψ : AddChar G ℂ} :
    ψ ∈ annihF S ↔ ∀ x ∈ S, ψ x = 1 := by simp [annihF]

omit [DecidableEq G] in
@[simp] lemma mem_closureF {S : Finset G} {x : G} : x ∈ closureF S ↔ x ∈ closureS S := by
  simp [closureF]

omit [DecidableEq G] in
lemma subset_closureF (S : Finset G) : S ⊆ closureF S := by
  intro x hx
  exact mem_closureF.2 (AddSubgroup.subset_closure (by exact_mod_cast hx))

/-- A character killing `S` kills the whole subgroup generated by `S`: the annihilator of a
finset only sees the subgroup it generates. -/
theorem annihF_eq_annih_closure (S : Finset G) : annihF S = annih (closureS S) := by
  ext ψ
  simp only [mem_annihF, mem_annih]
  constructor
  · intro h x hx
    refine AddSubgroup.closure_induction (p := fun y _ => ψ y = 1) ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ hx
    · intro y hy; exact h y (by exact_mod_cast hy)
    · exact ψ.map_zero_eq_one
    · intro a b _ _ ha hb; rw [ψ.map_add_eq_mul, ha, hb, one_mul]
    · intro a _ ha; rw [AddChar.map_neg_eq_inv, ha, inv_one]
  · intro h x hx
    exact h x (AddSubgroup.subset_closure (by exact_mod_cast hx))

omit [DecidableEq G] in
lemma closureF_eq_subFinset (S : Finset G) : closureF S = subFinset (closureS S) := rfl

/-! ## The fundamental character sum over `S^⊥` -/

/-- The engine of the converse: summing a character value over the annihilator of `S`.
This is `poisson_summation` for the subgroup `⟨S⟩` evaluated at a Dirac delta. -/
theorem card_closureF_mul_sum_annihF (S : Finset G) (y : G) :
    ((closureF S).card : ℂ) * ∑ ψ ∈ annihF S, conj (ψ y)
      = if y ∈ closureF S then (Fintype.card G : ℂ) else 0 := by
  have hp := poisson_summation (H := closureS S) (delta y)
  have hδ : ∑ x ∈ subFinset (closureS S), delta y x
      = if y ∈ closureF S then (1 : ℂ) else 0 := by
    simp only [delta]
    rw [Finset.sum_ite_eq' (subFinset (closureS S)) y (fun _ => (1 : ℂ))]
    simp [closureF]
  rw [hδ] at hp
  simp only [dft_delta] at hp
  rw [← annihF_eq_annih_closure] at hp
  rw [← closureF_eq_subFinset] at hp
  rw [← hp]
  by_cases hy : y ∈ closureF S <;> simp [hy]

/-- `|⟨S⟩| * |S^⊥| = |G|` for an arbitrary finset `S`: the annihilator of `S` has index
exactly the size of the subgroup generated by `S`. -/
theorem card_closure_mul_card_annihF (S : Finset G) :
    (closureF S).card * (annihF S).card = Fintype.card G := by
  rw [annihF_eq_annih_closure, closureF_eq_subFinset]
  exact card_subgroup_mul_card_annihilator

/-! ## The Poisson property, its defect, and the converse -/

/-- The Poisson summation property for an arbitrary finset `S ⊆ G`. -/
def PoissonSet (S : Finset G) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : G → ℂ, (Fintype.card G : ℂ) * ∑ x ∈ S, f x
    = (S.card : ℂ) * ∑ ψ ∈ annihF S, dft f ψ

/-- The Poisson defect of `S` at `f`: the difference of the two sides of `(P_S)`. -/
noncomputable def poissonDefect (S : Finset G) (f : G → ℂ) : ℂ :=
  (Fintype.card G : ℂ) * ∑ x ∈ S, f x - (S.card : ℂ) * ∑ ψ ∈ annihF S, dft f ψ

lemma poissonSet_iff_defect_zero (S : Finset G) :
    PoissonSet S ↔ ∀ f, poissonDefect S f = 0 := by
  simp [PoissonSet, poissonDefect, sub_eq_zero]

/-- **Exact defect formula.** Up to the positive factor `|⟨S⟩|`, the Poisson defect of `S`
at `f` measures exactly the failure of the average of `f` over `S` to agree with its average
over the subgroup `⟨S⟩` generated by `S`. -/
theorem poisson_defect_formula (S : Finset G) (f : G → ℂ) :
    ((closureF S).card : ℂ) * poissonDefect S f
      = (Fintype.card G : ℂ) *
          (((closureF S).card : ℂ) * ∑ x ∈ S, f x - (S.card : ℂ) * ∑ x ∈ closureF S, f x) := by
  have hp := poisson_summation (H := closureS S) f
  rw [← annihF_eq_annih_closure, ← closureF_eq_subFinset] at hp
  have key : ((closureF S).card : ℂ) * ((S.card : ℂ) * ∑ ψ ∈ annihF S, dft f ψ)
      = (S.card : ℂ) * ((Fintype.card G : ℂ) * ∑ x ∈ closureF S, f x) := by
    rw [hp]; ring
  simp only [poissonDefect, mul_sub]
  rw [key]
  ring

/-- **Strong converse (one test function suffices).** If the Poisson identity holds for the
single Dirac delta at one point `y₀ ∈ S`, then `S` is already the full subgroup it
generates. -/
theorem subgroup_of_poissonDelta (S : Finset G) {y₀ : G} (hy₀ : y₀ ∈ S)
    (h : (Fintype.card G : ℂ) * ∑ x ∈ S, delta y₀ x
        = (S.card : ℂ) * ∑ ψ ∈ annihF S, dft (delta y₀) ψ) :
    S = closureF S := by
  have hy₀H : y₀ ∈ closureF S := subset_closureF S hy₀
  -- The left side is `|G|`.
  have hL : ∑ x ∈ S, delta y₀ x = (1 : ℂ) := by
    simp only [delta]
    rw [Finset.sum_ite_eq' S y₀ (fun _ => (1 : ℂ))]
    simp [hy₀]
  -- Multiply the identity by `|⟨S⟩|` and use the fundamental character sum.
  have hcard : ((closureF S).card : ℂ) * (Fintype.card G : ℂ)
      = (S.card : ℂ) * (Fintype.card G : ℂ) := by
    have h2 : ((closureF S).card : ℂ) * ((Fintype.card G : ℂ) * ∑ x ∈ S, delta y₀ x)
        = ((closureF S).card : ℂ) * ((S.card : ℂ) * ∑ ψ ∈ annihF S, dft (delta y₀) ψ) := by
      rw [h]
    simp only [dft_delta, hL, mul_one] at h2
    rw [show ((closureF S).card : ℂ) * ((S.card : ℂ) * ∑ ψ ∈ annihF S, conj (ψ y₀))
          = (S.card : ℂ) * (((closureF S).card : ℂ) * ∑ ψ ∈ annihF S, conj (ψ y₀)) from by
        ring] at h2
    rw [card_closureF_mul_sum_annihF S y₀, if_pos hy₀H] at h2
    exact h2
  have hGne : (Fintype.card G : ℂ) ≠ 0 := by
    exact_mod_cast (Fintype.card_ne_zero (α := G))
  have hcards : (closureF S).card = S.card := by
    have := mul_right_cancel₀ hGne hcard
    exact_mod_cast this
  exact Finset.eq_of_subset_of_card_le (subset_closureF S) (le_of_eq hcards)

/-- **Converse of Poisson summation.** A nonempty finset satisfying the Poisson identity for
all `f` is a subgroup. -/
theorem subgroup_of_poissonSet {S : Finset G} (hS : S.Nonempty) (h : PoissonSet S) :
    S = closureF S := by
  obtain ⟨y₀, hy₀⟩ := hS
  exact subgroup_of_poissonDelta S hy₀ (h (delta y₀))

/-- The "if" direction, restated for a finset which happens to be a subgroup. -/
theorem poissonSet_of_eq_closureF {S : Finset G} (h : S = closureF S) : PoissonSet S := by
  intro f
  have hp := poisson_summation (H := closureS S) f
  rw [← annihF_eq_annih_closure, ← closureF_eq_subFinset] at hp
  calc (Fintype.card G : ℂ) * ∑ x ∈ S, f x
      = (Fintype.card G : ℂ) * ∑ x ∈ closureF S, f x := by rw [← h]
    _ = ((closureF S).card : ℂ) * ∑ ψ ∈ annihF S, dft f ψ := hp
    _ = (S.card : ℂ) * ∑ ψ ∈ annihF S, dft f ψ := by rw [← h]

/-- **Poisson summation characterises subgroups** (nonempty case). -/
theorem poissonSet_iff_subgroup {S : Finset G} (hS : S.Nonempty) :
    PoissonSet S ↔ ∃ H : AddSubgroup G, ∀ x, x ∈ S ↔ x ∈ H := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    refine ⟨closureS S, fun x => ⟨fun hx => mem_closureF.1 (subset_closureF S hx), fun hx => ?_⟩⟩
    rw [subgroup_of_poissonSet hS h]
    exact mem_closureF.2 hx
  · rintro ⟨H, hH⟩
    refine poissonSet_of_eq_closureF ?_
    have hsub : closureS S ≤ H := by
      rw [closureS, AddSubgroup.closure_le]
      intro x hx
      exact (hH x).1 (by exact_mod_cast hx)
    ext x
    constructor
    · intro hx; exact subset_closureF S hx
    · intro hx
      have hxH : x ∈ H := hsub (mem_closureF.1 hx)
      exact (hH x).2 hxH

/-- The empty set satisfies the Poisson identity vacuously: it is the unique exceptional
solution, and shows the nonemptiness hypothesis of `poissonSet_iff_subgroup` is sharp. -/
theorem poissonSet_empty : PoissonSet (∅ : Finset G) := by
  intro f
  simp

omit [Fintype G] [DecidableEq G] in
theorem empty_not_subgroup : ¬ ∃ H : AddSubgroup G, ∀ x, x ∈ (∅ : Finset G) ↔ x ∈ H := by
  rintro ⟨H, hH⟩
  exact absurd ((hH 0).2 H.zero_mem) (by simp)

/-- **Complete classification of Poisson sets**, with no hypothesis: `(P_S)` holds iff `S` is
empty or `S` is a subgroup. -/
theorem poissonSet_iff {S : Finset G} :
    PoissonSet S ↔ S = ∅ ∨ ∃ H : AddSubgroup G, ∀ x, x ∈ S ↔ x ∈ H := by
  rcases S.eq_empty_or_nonempty with rfl | hS
  · simp [poissonSet_empty]
  · rw [poissonSet_iff_subgroup hS]
    constructor
    · exact fun h => Or.inr h
    · rintro (rfl | h)
      · exact absurd hS (by simp)
      · exact h

/-- A purely combinatorial form of the classification: the Poisson identity holds for a
nonempty `S` exactly when `S` contains `0` and is closed under subtraction. -/
theorem poissonSet_iff_zero_mem_and_sub_mem {S : Finset G} (hS : S.Nonempty) :
    PoissonSet S ↔ ((0 : G) ∈ S ∧ ∀ x ∈ S, ∀ y ∈ S, x - y ∈ S) := by
  rw [poissonSet_iff_subgroup hS]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨H, hH⟩
    refine ⟨(hH 0).2 H.zero_mem, fun x hx y hy => (hH _).2 (H.sub_mem ((hH x).1 hx) ((hH y).1 hy))⟩
  · rintro ⟨h0, hsub⟩
    refine ⟨{ carrier := (S : Set G)
              add_mem' := ?_
              zero_mem' := by exact_mod_cast h0
              neg_mem' := ?_ }, ?_⟩
    · intro a b ha hb
      have hna : -b ∈ S := by
        have := hsub 0 h0 b (by exact_mod_cast hb)
        simpa using this
      have := hsub a (by exact_mod_cast ha) (-b) hna
      simpa using this
    · intro a ha
      have := hsub 0 h0 a (by exact_mod_cast ha)
      simpa using this
    · intro x
      simp

/-! ## Quantitative rigidity: there are no approximate Poisson sets -/

/-- **Gap theorem.** If `S` is nonempty and fails to be a subgroup, then a single Dirac delta
already witnesses a Poisson defect of modulus at least `|⟨S⟩| - |S| ≥ 1`.  Thus the Poisson
identity cannot hold even approximately for a non-subgroup. -/
theorem poisson_gap {S : Finset G} (hS : S.Nonempty) (hne : S ≠ closureF S) :
    ∃ y₀ ∈ S, ((closureF S).card - S.card : ℝ) ≤ ‖poissonDefect S (delta y₀)‖ := by
  obtain ⟨y₀, hy₀⟩ := hS
  refine ⟨y₀, hy₀, ?_⟩
  have hy₀H : y₀ ∈ closureF S := subset_closureF S hy₀
  have hsub : S ⊆ closureF S := subset_closureF S
  have hcard_lt : S.card < (closureF S).card := by
    rcases lt_or_eq_of_le (Finset.card_le_card hsub) with h | h
    · exact h
    · exact absurd (Finset.eq_of_subset_of_card_le hsub (le_of_eq h.symm)) hne
  -- Compute the defect exactly.
  have hL : ∑ x ∈ S, delta y₀ x = (1 : ℂ) := by
    simp only [delta]
    rw [Finset.sum_ite_eq' S y₀ (fun _ => (1 : ℂ))]
    simp [hy₀]
  have hHpos : (0 : ℝ) < ((closureF S).card : ℝ) := by
    have : 0 < (closureF S).card := lt_of_le_of_lt (Nat.zero_le _) hcard_lt
    exact_mod_cast this
  have hdiff : (0 : ℝ) ≤ ((closureF S).card : ℝ) - (S.card : ℝ) := by
    have : (S.card : ℝ) ≤ ((closureF S).card : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hcard_lt.le
    linarith
  have hkey : ((closureF S).card : ℂ) * poissonDefect S (delta y₀)
      = (Fintype.card G : ℂ) * (((closureF S).card : ℂ) - (S.card : ℂ)) := by
    rw [poisson_defect_formula S (delta y₀), hL]
    have h2 : ∑ x ∈ closureF S, delta y₀ x = (1 : ℂ) := by
      simp only [delta]
      rw [Finset.sum_ite_eq' (closureF S) y₀ (fun _ => (1 : ℂ))]
      simp [hy₀H]
    rw [h2]
    ring
  -- Take norms.
  have hnorm : ((closureF S).card : ℝ) * ‖poissonDefect S (delta y₀)‖
      = (Fintype.card G : ℝ) * (((closureF S).card : ℝ) - (S.card : ℝ)) := by
    have hkey' : ((closureF S).card : ℂ) * poissonDefect S (delta y₀)
        = (((Fintype.card G : ℝ) * (((closureF S).card : ℝ) - (S.card : ℝ)) : ℝ) : ℂ) := by
      rw [hkey]; push_cast; ring
    have hn := congrArg norm hkey'
    rw [norm_mul, Complex.norm_real, Real.norm_eq_abs,
      abs_of_nonneg (by positivity : (0:ℝ) ≤ (Fintype.card G : ℝ) *
        (((closureF S).card : ℝ) - (S.card : ℝ)))] at hn
    simpa using hn
  -- `|G| ≥ |⟨S⟩|`, so dividing by `|⟨S⟩|` gives the claim.
  have hGH : ((closureF S).card : ℝ) ≤ (Fintype.card G : ℝ) := by
    have : (closureF S).card ≤ Fintype.card G := by
      simpa using Finset.card_le_card (Finset.subset_univ (closureF S))
    exact_mod_cast this
  refine le_of_mul_le_mul_left ?_ hHpos
  calc ((closureF S).card : ℝ) * (((closureF S).card : ℝ) - (S.card : ℝ))
      ≤ (Fintype.card G : ℝ) * (((closureF S).card : ℝ) - (S.card : ℝ)) :=
        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hGH hdiff
    _ = ((closureF S).card : ℝ) * ‖poissonDefect S (delta y₀)‖ := hnorm.symm

end FourierFA


/- ===== Catalog/Pythagorean/FourierPoissonUncertainty.lean ===== -/

/-
# Poisson sets, uncertainty extremality, and rigidity of the Poisson constant

This file continues `Catalog.Pythagorean.FourierPoissonConverse`, where the converse of
finite Poisson summation was established, and links it to the Donoho–Stark uncertainty
principle of `Catalog.Shared.FourierFiniteAbelian`.

For an arbitrary finset `S ⊆ G` write `S^⊥ = annihF S` for its annihilator and `1_S` for its
indicator.  The two "dual" size estimates

  `|S| * |S^⊥| ≤ |G| ≤ |S| * |supp (1_S)^|`         (`card_mul_card_annihF_le`,
                                                     `card_le_card_mul_card_supp_dft_indicF`)

sandwich `|G|`, the left one coming from the subgroup generated by `S` and the right one
being the uncertainty principle applied to `1_S`.  Main results:

* `FourierFA.poissonSet_iff_card_mul_card_annihF` : for nonempty `S`, Poisson summation holds
  for `S` **iff** the left estimate is an equality, `|S| * |S^⊥| = |G|`.
* `FourierFA.poissonSet_iff_supp_dft_indicF_eq_annihF` : ... **iff** the Fourier support of
  `1_S` is exactly `S^⊥`, i.e. iff `S` is extremal for the uncertainty principle in the strong
  (set-theoretic) sense.
* `FourierFA.poisson_constant_unique` : **rigidity of the Poisson constant.** If *some*
  constant `c` makes `|G| ∑_{x ∈ S} f = c ∑_{ψ ∈ S^⊥} f̂` valid for all `f` and `S ≠ ∅`, then
  `S` is a subgroup *and* `c = |S|`; the constant cannot be renormalised away.
* Concrete instances over `ZMod 4`, `ZMod 8` (the squares mod 4 and mod 8, i.e. the residue
  sets governing Pythagorean triples, are *not* Poisson sets; the even residues are).
-/

import Mathlib
import Pythagorean.FourierPoissonConverse

open Finset Fintype ComplexConjugate
open scoped Classical

namespace FourierFA

variable {G : Type*} [AddCommGroup G] [Fintype G] [DecidableEq G]

/-! ## The indicator of an arbitrary finset -/

/-- The indicator function of an arbitrary finset `S ⊆ G`. -/
noncomputable def indicF (S : Finset G) : G → ℂ := fun x => if x ∈ S then 1 else 0

omit [AddCommGroup G] in
@[simp] lemma supp_indicF (S : Finset G) : supp (indicF S) = S := by
  ext x
  simp [mem_supp, indicF]

lemma dft_indicF_apply (S : Finset G) (ψ : AddChar G ℂ) :
    dft (indicF S) ψ = ∑ x ∈ S, conj (ψ x) := by
  rw [dft]
  have h : ∀ x : G, conj (ψ x) * indicF S x = if x ∈ S then conj (ψ x) else 0 := by
    intro x; by_cases hx : x ∈ S <;> simp [indicF, hx]
  simp_rw [h]
  rw [Finset.sum_ite_mem, Finset.univ_inter]

lemma dft_indicF_of_mem_annihF {S : Finset G} {ψ : AddChar G ℂ} (h : ψ ∈ annihF S) :
    dft (indicF S) ψ = (S.card : ℂ) := by
  rw [dft_indicF_apply]
  rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun x hx => by rw [mem_annihF.1 h x hx, map_one])]
  simp

/-- The annihilator of `S` is always contained in the Fourier support of `1_S`. -/
lemma annihF_subset_supp_dft_indicF {S : Finset G} (hS : S.Nonempty) :
    annihF S ⊆ supp (dft (indicF S)) := by
  intro ψ hψ
  rw [mem_supp, dft_indicF_of_mem_annihF hψ]
  exact_mod_cast (Finset.card_pos.2 hS).ne'

/-! ## The two dual size estimates -/

/-- **Lower estimate**: `|S| * |S^⊥| ≤ |G|` for every finset `S`, with the annihilator
of `S` playing the role of the dual object. -/
theorem card_mul_card_annihF_le (S : Finset G) :
    S.card * (annihF S).card ≤ Fintype.card G := by
  have h := card_closure_mul_card_annihF S
  have hle : S.card ≤ (closureF S).card := Finset.card_le_card (subset_closureF S)
  calc S.card * (annihF S).card ≤ (closureF S).card * (annihF S).card :=
        Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ hle
    _ = Fintype.card G := h

/-- **Upper estimate**: the Donoho–Stark uncertainty principle applied to `1_S`. -/
theorem card_le_card_mul_card_supp_dft_indicF {S : Finset G} (hS : S.Nonempty) :
    Fintype.card G ≤ S.card * (supp (dft (indicF S))).card := by
  obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := hS
  have hne : indicF S ≠ 0 := by
    intro h
    have : indicF S y = 0 := by rw [h]; rfl
    rw [indicF, if_pos hy] at this
    exact one_ne_zero this
  have := uncertainty (indicF S) hne
  rwa [supp_indicF] at this

/-! ## Poisson sets are exactly the uncertainty extremals -/

/-- **Poisson summation ⟺ extremality in `|S| * |S^⊥| ≤ |G|`.** -/
theorem poissonSet_iff_card_mul_card_annihF {S : Finset G} (hS : S.Nonempty) :
    PoissonSet S ↔ S.card * (annihF S).card = Fintype.card G := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    have hSc := subgroup_of_poissonSet hS h
    have hprod := card_closure_mul_card_annihF S
    rwa [← hSc] at hprod
  · intro h
    have hprod := card_closure_mul_card_annihF S
    have hApos : 0 < (annihF S).card := by
      rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos (annihF S).card with h0 | hpos
      · rw [h0, Nat.mul_zero] at h
        exact absurd h.symm (Fintype.card_ne_zero (α := G))
      · exact hpos
    have hcards : S.card = (closureF S).card :=
      Nat.eq_of_mul_eq_mul_right hApos (by rw [h, hprod])
    exact poissonSet_of_eq_closureF
      (Finset.eq_of_subset_of_card_le (subset_closureF S) (le_of_eq hcards.symm))

/-- **Poisson summation ⟺ the Fourier support of `1_S` is exactly `S^⊥`.**  For a general
finset the containment `S^⊥ ⊆ supp (1_S)^` may be strict; equality happens precisely for
subgroups. -/
theorem poissonSet_iff_supp_dft_indicF_eq_annihF {S : Finset G} (hS : S.Nonempty) :
    PoissonSet S ↔ supp (dft (indicF S)) = annihF S := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    have hSc := subgroup_of_poissonSet hS h
    have hfun : indicF S = indic (closureS S) := by
      funext x
      by_cases hx : x ∈ S
      · have hx' : x ∈ closureS S := mem_closureF.1 (subset_closureF S hx)
        simp [indicF, indic, hx, hx']
      · have hx' : x ∉ closureS S := by
          intro hc
          exact hx (by rw [hSc]; exact mem_closureF.2 hc)
        simp [indicF, indic, hx, hx']
    rw [hfun, supp_dft_indic, annihF_eq_annih_closure]
  · intro h
    rw [poissonSet_iff_card_mul_card_annihF hS]
    have h1 : Fintype.card G ≤ S.card * (annihF S).card := by
      have := card_le_card_mul_card_supp_dft_indicF hS
      rwa [h] at this
    exact le_antisymm (card_mul_card_annihF_le S) h1

/-! ## Rigidity of the Poisson constant -/

/-- **The Poisson constant is forced.**  Suppose that for a nonempty finset `S` there exists
*any* complex constant `c` with `|G| ∑_{x ∈ S} f x = c ∑_{ψ ∈ S^⊥} f̂ ψ` for all `f`.  Then
`S` is a subgroup and `c` is necessarily `|S|`.  So the Poisson identity cannot be rescued for
non-subgroups by tuning the normalising constant. -/
theorem poisson_constant_unique {S : Finset G} (hS : S.Nonempty) (c : ℂ)
    (h : ∀ f : G → ℂ, (Fintype.card G : ℂ) * ∑ x ∈ S, f x
      = c * ∑ ψ ∈ annihF S, dft f ψ) :
    S = closureF S ∧ c = (S.card : ℂ) := by
  have hGne : (Fintype.card G : ℂ) ≠ 0 := by
    exact_mod_cast (Fintype.card_ne_zero (α := G))
  -- Step 1: testing at a delta inside `S` forces `c = |⟨S⟩|`.
  obtain ⟨y₀, hy₀⟩ := hS
  have hdelta : ∀ y : G, ∑ x ∈ S, delta y x = if y ∈ S then (1 : ℂ) else 0 := by
    intro y
    simp only [delta]
    rw [Finset.sum_ite_eq' S y (fun _ => (1 : ℂ))]
  have hc : c * (Fintype.card G : ℂ) = ((closureF S).card : ℂ) * (Fintype.card G : ℂ) := by
    have h0 := h (delta y₀)
    simp only [dft_delta, hdelta y₀, if_pos hy₀, mul_one] at h0
    have h1 : ((closureF S).card : ℂ) * (Fintype.card G : ℂ)
        = ((closureF S).card : ℂ) * (c * ∑ ψ ∈ annihF S, conj (ψ y₀)) := by
      rw [← h0]
    rw [show ((closureF S).card : ℂ) * (c * ∑ ψ ∈ annihF S, conj (ψ y₀))
          = c * (((closureF S).card : ℂ) * ∑ ψ ∈ annihF S, conj (ψ y₀)) from by ring,
      card_closureF_mul_sum_annihF S y₀, if_pos (subset_closureF S hy₀)] at h1
    linear_combination -h1
  have hcH : c = ((closureF S).card : ℂ) := mul_right_cancel₀ hGne hc
  -- Step 2: every element of `⟨S⟩` must already lie in `S`.
  have hsubset : closureF S ⊆ S := by
    intro y hy
    by_contra hyS
    have h0 := h (delta y)
    simp only [dft_delta, hdelta y, if_neg hyS, mul_zero] at h0
    have h1 : ((closureF S).card : ℂ) * 0
        = ((closureF S).card : ℂ) * (c * ∑ ψ ∈ annihF S, conj (ψ y)) := by
      rw [← h0]
    rw [show ((closureF S).card : ℂ) * (c * ∑ ψ ∈ annihF S, conj (ψ y))
          = c * (((closureF S).card : ℂ) * ∑ ψ ∈ annihF S, conj (ψ y)) from by ring,
      card_closureF_mul_sum_annihF S y, if_pos hy, hcH] at h1
    have h2 : ((closureF S).card : ℂ) * (Fintype.card G : ℂ) = 0 := by
      rw [mul_zero] at h1; exact h1.symm
    rcases mul_eq_zero.1 h2 with hz | hz
    · have : (closureF S).card = 0 := by exact_mod_cast hz
      rw [Finset.card_eq_zero] at this
      exact absurd hy (by rw [this]; simp)
    · exact hGne hz
  have hSeq : S = closureF S :=
    Finset.Subset.antisymm (subset_closureF S) hsubset
  exact ⟨hSeq, by rw [hcH, ← hSeq]⟩

/-! ## Concrete instances

The squares modulo `4` are `{0, 1}` and the squares modulo `8` are `{0, 1, 4}`; these are the
residue sets that control the classical parametrisation of Pythagorean triples.  Neither is a
subgroup, hence neither satisfies Poisson summation, while the even residues mod `8` do. -/

/-- The set of squares mod `4` is not a Poisson set. -/
theorem not_poissonSet_squares_zmod4 : ¬ PoissonSet ({0, 1} : Finset (ZMod 4)) := by
  intro h
  have hS : ({0, 1} : Finset (ZMod 4)).Nonempty := ⟨0, by decide⟩
  rw [poissonSet_iff_zero_mem_and_sub_mem hS] at h
  have := h.2 0 (by decide) 1 (by decide)
  revert this
  decide

/-- The set of squares mod `8` is not a Poisson set. -/
theorem not_poissonSet_squares_zmod8 : ¬ PoissonSet ({0, 1, 4} : Finset (ZMod 8)) := by
  intro h
  have hS : ({0, 1, 4} : Finset (ZMod 8)).Nonempty := ⟨0, by decide⟩
  rw [poissonSet_iff_zero_mem_and_sub_mem hS] at h
  have := h.2 1 (by decide) 4 (by decide)
  revert this
  decide

/-- The even residues mod `8` do form a Poisson set. -/
theorem poissonSet_even_zmod8 : PoissonSet ({0, 2, 4, 6} : Finset (ZMod 8)) := by
  have hS : ({0, 2, 4, 6} : Finset (ZMod 8)).Nonempty := ⟨0, by decide⟩
  rw [poissonSet_iff_zero_mem_and_sub_mem hS]
  exact ⟨by decide, by decide⟩

end FourierFA


/- ===== Catalog/Pythagorean/FourierPoissonCoset.lean ===== -/

/-
# Affine (coset) Poisson summation and its converse

`Catalog.Pythagorean.FourierPoissonConverse` shows that the *exact* Poisson identity
singles out subgroups.  Subgroups are however not translation invariant, whereas the two
sides of Poisson summation transform very predictably under translation: replacing `f` by
`f (x₀ + ·)` multiplies each Fourier coefficient by the phase `ψ x₀`.

This file develops the resulting **affine** theory: the phase-twisted identity

  `|G| * ∑_{x ∈ S} f x = |S| * ∑_{ψ ∈ (S - x₀)^⊥} ψ x₀ * f̂ ψ`                    (P_{S,x₀})

and proves that it characterises **cosets** exactly as `(P_S)` characterises subgroups.

Main results:

* `FourierFA.dft_translate` : `(f (x₀ + ·))^ ψ = ψ x₀ * f̂ ψ`.
* `FourierFA.cosetPoissonSet_iff_poissonSet_translate` : `(P_{S,x₀})` for `S` is exactly
  `(P_T)` for the translate `T = S - x₀`.
* `FourierFA.cosetPoissonSet_iff_coset` : for nonempty `S` and `x₀ ∈ S`, `(P_{S,x₀})` holds
  **iff** `S` is a coset of a subgroup, `S = x₀ + H`.
* `FourierFA.cosetPoissonSet_of_coset` : the "if" direction, i.e. affine Poisson summation.
* `FourierFA.not_cosetPoissonSet_squares_zmod8` : the squares mod `8` are not even a coset,
  so no choice of base point rescues Poisson summation for them.
-/

import Mathlib
import Pythagorean.FourierPoissonUncertainty

open Finset Fintype ComplexConjugate
open scoped Classical

namespace FourierFA

variable {G : Type*} [AddCommGroup G] [Fintype G] [DecidableEq G]

/-! ## Translation and the Fourier transform -/

omit [DecidableEq G] in
/-- Translating the argument multiplies the Fourier coefficients by a phase. -/
theorem dft_translate (f : G → ℂ) (x₀ : G) (ψ : AddChar G ℂ) :
    dft (fun y => f (x₀ + y)) ψ = ψ x₀ * dft f ψ := by
  rw [dft, dft, Finset.mul_sum]
  rw [← Fintype.sum_equiv (Equiv.addLeft x₀) (fun y => conj (ψ y) * f (x₀ + y))
      (fun z => ψ x₀ * (conj (ψ z) * f z)) ?_]
  intro y
  have hzy : (Equiv.addLeft x₀) y = x₀ + y := rfl
  rw [hzy]
  have : ψ (x₀ + y) = ψ x₀ * ψ y := ψ.map_add_eq_mul x₀ y
  have hnorm : ψ x₀ * conj (ψ x₀) = 1 := by
    rw [← AddChar.map_neg_eq_conj, ← ψ.map_add_eq_mul]
    simp
  calc conj (ψ y) * f (x₀ + y)
      = (ψ x₀ * conj (ψ x₀)) * (conj (ψ y) * f (x₀ + y)) := by rw [hnorm, one_mul]
    _ = ψ x₀ * (conj (ψ x₀ * ψ y) * f (x₀ + y)) := by rw [map_mul]; ring
    _ = ψ x₀ * (conj (ψ (x₀ + y)) * f (x₀ + y)) := by rw [this]

/-! ## The affine Poisson property -/

/-- The translate `S - x₀` of a finset. -/
noncomputable def translateF (S : Finset G) (x₀ : G) : Finset G := S.image (fun x => x - x₀)

omit [Fintype G] in
@[simp] lemma mem_translateF {S : Finset G} {x₀ y : G} :
    y ∈ translateF S x₀ ↔ y + x₀ ∈ S := by
  simp only [translateF, Finset.mem_image]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩; simpa using hx
  · intro h; exact ⟨y + x₀, h, by abel⟩

omit [Fintype G] in
@[simp] lemma card_translateF (S : Finset G) (x₀ : G) :
    (translateF S x₀).card = S.card :=
  Finset.card_image_of_injective _ (fun a b hab => by
    have := congrArg (· + x₀) hab
    simpa using this)

/-- The phase-twisted (affine) Poisson property with base point `x₀`. -/
def CosetPoissonSet (S : Finset G) (x₀ : G) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : G → ℂ, (Fintype.card G : ℂ) * ∑ x ∈ S, f x
    = (S.card : ℂ) * ∑ ψ ∈ annihF (translateF S x₀), ψ x₀ * dft f ψ

omit [Fintype G] in
lemma sum_translateF (S : Finset G) (x₀ : G) (f : G → ℂ) :
    ∑ y ∈ translateF S x₀, f (x₀ + y) = ∑ x ∈ S, f x := by
  rw [translateF, Finset.sum_image (fun a _ b _ hab => by
    have := congrArg (· + x₀) hab
    simpa using this)]
  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun x _ => by rw [show x₀ + (x - x₀) = x by abel]

/-- **The affine identity is the plain identity for the translate.** -/
theorem cosetPoissonSet_iff_poissonSet_translate (S : Finset G) (x₀ : G) :
    CosetPoissonSet S x₀ ↔ PoissonSet (translateF S x₀) := by
  constructor
  · intro h g
    have hf := h (fun x => g (x - x₀))
    rw [card_translateF]
    have hL : ∑ x ∈ S, g (x - x₀) = ∑ y ∈ translateF S x₀, g y := by
      rw [← sum_translateF S x₀ (fun x => g (x - x₀))]
      exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun y _ => by rw [show x₀ + y - x₀ = y by abel]
    have hR : ∀ ψ : AddChar G ℂ, ψ x₀ * dft (fun x => g (x - x₀)) ψ = dft g ψ := by
      intro ψ
      have : (fun y => (fun x => g (x - x₀)) (x₀ + y)) = g := by
        funext y; simp only; rw [show x₀ + y - x₀ = y by abel]
      have h2 := dft_translate (fun x => g (x - x₀)) x₀ ψ
      rw [this] at h2
      exact h2.symm
    rw [hL] at hf
    rw [hf]
    exact congrArg _ (Finset.sum_congr rfl fun ψ _ => hR ψ)
  · intro h f
    have hg := h (fun y => f (x₀ + y))
    rw [card_translateF, sum_translateF S x₀ f] at hg
    rw [hg]
    exact congrArg _ (Finset.sum_congr rfl fun ψ _ => (dft_translate f x₀ ψ))

/-- **Affine Poisson summation.**  Every coset `S = x₀ + H` of a subgroup satisfies the
phase-twisted identity with base point `x₀`. -/
theorem cosetPoissonSet_of_coset {S : Finset G} {x₀ : G} {H : AddSubgroup G}
    (hH : ∀ x, x ∈ S ↔ x - x₀ ∈ H) : CosetPoissonSet S x₀ := by
  rw [cosetPoissonSet_iff_poissonSet_translate]
  refine (poissonSet_iff).2 (Or.inr ⟨H, fun y => ?_⟩)
  rw [mem_translateF, hH (y + x₀), show y + x₀ - x₀ = y by abel]

/-- **Converse of affine Poisson summation: the identity characterises cosets.** -/
theorem cosetPoissonSet_iff_coset {S : Finset G} {x₀ : G} (hx₀ : x₀ ∈ S) :
    CosetPoissonSet S x₀ ↔ ∃ H : AddSubgroup G, ∀ x, x ∈ S ↔ x - x₀ ∈ H := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    rw [cosetPoissonSet_iff_poissonSet_translate] at h
    have hne : (translateF S x₀).Nonempty := ⟨0, mem_translateF.2 (by simpa using hx₀)⟩
    obtain ⟨H, hH⟩ := (poissonSet_iff_subgroup hne).1 h
    refine ⟨H, fun x => ?_⟩
    have := hH (x - x₀)
    rw [mem_translateF, show x - x₀ + x₀ = x by abel] at this
    exact this
  · rintro ⟨H, hH⟩
    exact cosetPoissonSet_of_coset hH

/-- Cosets are the only sets for which *some* base point works. -/
theorem exists_cosetPoissonSet_iff_coset {S : Finset G} :
    (∃ x₀ ∈ S, CosetPoissonSet S x₀)
      ↔ ∃ (x₀ : G) (H : AddSubgroup G), x₀ ∈ S ∧ ∀ x, x ∈ S ↔ x - x₀ ∈ H := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨x₀, hx₀, h⟩
    obtain ⟨H, hH⟩ := (cosetPoissonSet_iff_coset hx₀).1 h
    exact ⟨x₀, H, hx₀, hH⟩
  · rintro ⟨x₀, H, hx₀, hH⟩
    exact ⟨x₀, hx₀, cosetPoissonSet_of_coset hH⟩

/-- The squares mod `8` are not a coset either: no base point makes the affine Poisson
identity true for them. -/
theorem not_cosetPoissonSet_squares_zmod8 :
    ∀ x₀ ∈ ({0, 1, 4} : Finset (ZMod 8)), ¬ CosetPoissonSet ({0, 1, 4} : Finset (ZMod 8)) x₀ := by
  intro x₀ hx₀ h
  obtain ⟨H, hH⟩ := (cosetPoissonSet_iff_coset hx₀).1 h
  -- `S - x₀` would have to be a subgroup, but it is never closed under subtraction.
  have hsub : ∀ x ∈ ({0, 1, 4} : Finset (ZMod 8)), ∀ y ∈ ({0, 1, 4} : Finset (ZMod 8)),
      x - y + x₀ ∈ ({0, 1, 4} : Finset (ZMod 8)) := by
    intro x hx y hy
    refine (hH _).2 ?_
    have hx' : x - x₀ ∈ H := (hH x).1 hx
    have hy' : y - x₀ ∈ H := (hH y).1 hy
    have : x - y + x₀ - x₀ = (x - x₀) - (y - x₀) := by abel
    rw [this]
    exact H.sub_mem hx' hy'
  have h1 := hsub 1 (by decide) 4 (by decide)
  have h4 := hsub 4 (by decide) 1 (by decide)
  have hfin : ∀ z : ZMod 8, z ∈ ({0, 1, 4} : Finset (ZMod 8)) →
      1 - 4 + z ∈ ({0, 1, 4} : Finset (ZMod 8)) →
      4 - 1 + z ∈ ({0, 1, 4} : Finset (ZMod 8)) → False := by decide
  exact hfin x₀ hx₀ h1 h4

end FourierFA


/- ===== Catalog/Pythagorean/FourierPoissonCounting.lean ===== -/

/-
# The Poisson spectrum of a finite abelian group

The converse of Poisson summation (`Catalog.Pythagorean.FourierPoissonConverse`) turns the
*analytic* condition `PoissonSet S` into a *decidable combinatorial* condition: `S` is empty,
or `S` contains `0` and is closed under subtraction.  This file exploits that reduction.

Main results:

* `FourierFA.poissonSet_iff_comb` : the decidable criterion, valid for every finset of every
  finite abelian group.
* Complete determination of the **Poisson spectrum** (the family of all Poisson sets) of
  `ZMod 4`, `ZMod 5`, `ZMod 6`, `ZMod 8` and of the Klein four-group `ZMod 2 × ZMod 2`,
  each verified exhaustively over all `2^{|G|}` subsets.
* `FourierFA.card_poissonSets_zmod6`, `FourierFA.card_poissonSets_zmod8` : the number of
  nonempty Poisson sets of `ZMod n` equals the number of divisors of `n` (`n = 6, 8`).
* `FourierFA.poissonSpectrum_distinguishes_zmod4_klein` : `ZMod 4` and the Klein four-group
  have the same order but a different number of Poisson sets (`4` versus `6`).  Hence the
  Poisson spectrum is a genuine isomorphism invariant, not a function of `|G|`: Poisson
  summation "sees" the isomorphism type of the group.
-/

import Mathlib
import Pythagorean.FourierPoissonCoset

open Finset Fintype ComplexConjugate
open scoped Classical

namespace FourierFA

variable {G : Type*} [AddCommGroup G] [Fintype G] [DecidableEq G]

/-- **Decidable criterion for Poisson summation.**  Combining the classification of Poisson
sets with the finiteness of `G`, the analytic identity `(P_S)` is equivalent to a finite,
checkable combinatorial condition. -/
theorem poissonSet_iff_comb (S : Finset G) :
    PoissonSet S ↔ (S = ∅ ∨ ((0 : G) ∈ S ∧ ∀ x ∈ S, ∀ y ∈ S, x - y ∈ S)) := by
  rcases S.eq_empty_or_nonempty with rfl | hS
  · simp [poissonSet_empty]
  · rw [poissonSet_iff_zero_mem_and_sub_mem hS]
    constructor
    · exact fun h => Or.inr h
    · rintro (rfl | h)
      · exact absurd hS (by simp)
      · exact h

/-! ## The Poisson spectrum of small groups

Each statement below is an exhaustive verification over all subsets of the group. -/

set_option maxRecDepth 40000 in
/-- The Poisson sets of `ZMod 4` are `∅`, `{0}`, `{0,2}` and `ZMod 4`. -/
theorem poissonSet_zmod4_iff (S : Finset (ZMod 4)) :
    PoissonSet S ↔ (S = ∅ ∨ S = {0} ∨ S = {0, 2} ∨ S = Finset.univ) := by
  rw [poissonSet_iff_comb]
  revert S
  decide

set_option maxRecDepth 40000 in
/-- `ZMod 5` has prime order, so its only Poisson sets are the trivial ones. -/
theorem poissonSet_zmod5_iff (S : Finset (ZMod 5)) :
    PoissonSet S ↔ (S = ∅ ∨ S = {0} ∨ S = Finset.univ) := by
  rw [poissonSet_iff_comb]
  revert S
  decide

set_option maxRecDepth 40000 in
/-- The Poisson sets of `ZMod 6`. -/
theorem poissonSet_zmod6_iff (S : Finset (ZMod 6)) :
    PoissonSet S ↔ (S = ∅ ∨ S = {0} ∨ S = {0, 3} ∨ S = {0, 2, 4} ∨ S = Finset.univ) := by
  rw [poissonSet_iff_comb]
  revert S
  decide

set_option maxRecDepth 100000 in
/-- The Poisson sets of `ZMod 8`.  In particular `{0,1,4}` (the squares mod `8`) is absent,
reproving `not_poissonSet_squares_zmod8` by exhaustion. -/
theorem poissonSet_zmod8_iff (S : Finset (ZMod 8)) :
    PoissonSet S ↔ (S = ∅ ∨ S = {0} ∨ S = {0, 4} ∨ S = {0, 2, 4, 6} ∨ S = Finset.univ) := by
  rw [poissonSet_iff_comb]
  revert S
  decide

set_option maxRecDepth 40000 in
set_option synthInstance.maxSize 1000 in
/-- The Poisson sets of the Klein four-group: there are **six**, one more than the number of
subsets of `ZMod 4` that are Poisson, although both groups have order `4`. -/
theorem poissonSet_klein_iff (S : Finset (ZMod 2 × ZMod 2)) :
    PoissonSet S ↔ (S = ∅ ∨ S = {0} ∨ S = {0, (1, 0)} ∨ S = {0, (0, 1)} ∨ S = {0, (1, 1)}
      ∨ S = Finset.univ) := by
  rw [poissonSet_iff_comb]
  revert S
  decide

/-! ## Counting: the Poisson spectrum is an isomorphism invariant -/

set_option maxRecDepth 40000 in
/-- `ZMod 4` has exactly `4` Poisson sets. -/
theorem card_poissonSets_zmod4 :
    ((Finset.univ : Finset (Finset (ZMod 4))).filter (fun S => PoissonSet S)).card = 4 := by
  have hcongr : ((Finset.univ : Finset (Finset (ZMod 4))).filter (fun S => PoissonSet S))
      = ((Finset.univ : Finset (Finset (ZMod 4))).filter
          (fun S => S = ∅ ∨ S = {0} ∨ S = {0, 2} ∨ S = Finset.univ)) :=
    Finset.filter_congr (fun S _ => poissonSet_zmod4_iff S)
  rw [hcongr]
  decide

set_option maxRecDepth 40000 in
set_option synthInstance.maxSize 1000 in
/-- The Klein four-group has exactly `6` Poisson sets. -/
theorem card_poissonSets_klein :
    ((Finset.univ : Finset (Finset (ZMod 2 × ZMod 2))).filter (fun S => PoissonSet S)).card
      = 6 := by
  have hcongr :
      ((Finset.univ : Finset (Finset (ZMod 2 × ZMod 2))).filter (fun S => PoissonSet S))
      = ((Finset.univ : Finset (Finset (ZMod 2 × ZMod 2))).filter
          (fun S => S = ∅ ∨ S = {0} ∨ S = {0, (1, 0)} ∨ S = {0, (0, 1)} ∨ S = {0, (1, 1)}
            ∨ S = Finset.univ)) :=
    Finset.filter_congr (fun S _ => poissonSet_klein_iff S)
  rw [hcongr]
  decide

set_option synthInstance.maxSize 1000 in
/-- **The Poisson spectrum separates groups of equal order.**  `ZMod 4` and `ZMod 2 × ZMod 2`
both have four elements, yet they admit a different number of Poisson sets.  Consequently the
number of exact Poisson summation formulas available on a finite abelian group is not
determined by its cardinality; it is a genuine isomorphism invariant. -/
theorem poissonSpectrum_distinguishes_zmod4_klein :
    Fintype.card (ZMod 4) = Fintype.card (ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) ∧
    ((Finset.univ : Finset (Finset (ZMod 4))).filter (fun S => PoissonSet S)).card
      ≠ ((Finset.univ : Finset (Finset (ZMod 2 × ZMod 2))).filter
          (fun S => PoissonSet S)).card := by
  refine ⟨by simp, ?_⟩
  rw [card_poissonSets_zmod4, card_poissonSets_klein]
  omega

set_option maxRecDepth 40000 in
/-- For `ZMod 6` the nonempty Poisson sets are in bijection with the divisors of `6`. -/
theorem card_poissonSets_zmod6 :
    ((Finset.univ : Finset (Finset (ZMod 6))).filter (fun S => S.Nonempty ∧ PoissonSet S)).card
      = (Nat.divisors 6).card := by
  have hcongr :
      ((Finset.univ : Finset (Finset (ZMod 6))).filter (fun S => S.Nonempty ∧ PoissonSet S))
      = ((Finset.univ : Finset (Finset (ZMod 6))).filter
          (fun S => S = {0} ∨ S = {0, 3} ∨ S = {0, 2, 4} ∨ S = Finset.univ)) := by
    refine Finset.filter_congr (fun S _ => ?_)
    rw [poissonSet_zmod6_iff S]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨hne, (rfl | h)⟩
      · exact absurd hne (by simp)
      · exact h
    · intro h
      refine ⟨?_, Or.inr h⟩
      rcases h with rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl <;> exact ⟨0, by decide⟩
  rw [hcongr]
  decide

set_option maxRecDepth 100000 in
/-- For `ZMod 8` the nonempty Poisson sets are in bijection with the divisors of `8`. -/

  have hcongr :

    refine Finset.filter_congr (fun S _ => ?_)
    rw [poissonSet_zmod8_iff S]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨hne, (rfl | h)⟩
      · exact absurd hne (by simp)

      refine ⟨?_, Or.inr h⟩

/- ===== Catalog/Pythagorean/FourierPoissonLattice.lean ===== -/

/-
# The Poisson spectrum *is* the subgroup lattice

The classification of Poisson sets (`Catalog.Pythagorean.FourierPoissonConverse`) is upgraded
here from a pointwise statement to a structural one: the family of nonempty Poisson sets of a
finite abelian group `G`, ordered by inclusion, is canonically isomorphic to the lattice of
subgroups of `G`.

Main results:

* `FourierFA.poissonSetEquivSubgroup` : an explicit bijection
  `{S : Finset G // S.Nonempty ∧ PoissonSet S} ≃ AddSubgroup G`, given by `S ↦ ⟨S⟩` with
  inverse `H ↦ H`.
* `FourierFA.card_poissonSets_eq_card_subgroups` : consequently the number of exact Poisson
  summation formulas on `G` equals the number of subgroups of `G`.  (For `G = ZMod n` this is
  the number of divisors of `n`; see `Catalog.Pythagorean.FourierPoissonCounting` for the
  exhaustively verified small cases.)
* `FourierFA.poissonSet_subset_iff_le` : the bijection is an order isomorphism.
* `FourierFA.poissonSet_inter` : Poisson sets are closed under intersection (the lattice meet),
  whereas `FourierFA.not_poissonSet_union_example` exhibits a union of two Poisson sets that is
  not Poisson — the family is a meet-semilattice but not a sublattice of the Boolean algebra
  of subsets.
-/

import Mathlib
import Pythagorean.FourierPoissonCounting

open Finset Fintype ComplexConjugate
open scoped Classical

namespace FourierFA

variable {G : Type*} [AddCommGroup G] [Fintype G] [DecidableEq G]

omit [DecidableEq G] in
/-- The subgroup generated by the carrier of a subgroup is the subgroup itself. -/
lemma closureS_subFinset (H : AddSubgroup G) : closureS (subFinset H) = H := by
  have hset : ((subFinset H : Finset G) : Set G) = (H : Set G) := by
    ext x
    simp [mem_subFinset]
  rw [closureS, hset, AddSubgroup.closure_eq]

lemma poissonSet_subFinset (H : AddSubgroup G) : PoissonSet (subFinset H) := by
  refine poissonSet_of_eq_closureF ?_
  rw [closureF, closureS_subFinset]

omit [DecidableEq G] in
lemma nonempty_subFinset (H : AddSubgroup G) : (subFinset H).Nonempty :=
  ⟨0, mem_subFinset.2 H.zero_mem⟩

/-- **The Poisson spectrum is the subgroup lattice.**  Nonempty Poisson sets correspond
bijectively to subgroups, via `S ↦ ⟨S⟩` and `H ↦ H`. -/
noncomputable def poissonSetEquivSubgroup :
    {S : Finset G // S.Nonempty ∧ PoissonSet S} ≃ AddSubgroup G where
  toFun S := closureS S.1
  invFun H := ⟨subFinset H, nonempty_subFinset H, poissonSet_subFinset H⟩
  left_inv := by
    rintro ⟨S, hne, hP⟩
    refine Subtype.ext ?_
    have := subgroup_of_poissonSet hne hP
    simpa [closureF] using this.symm
  right_inv := by
    intro H
    exact closureS_subFinset H

/-- The number of exact Poisson summation formulas available on `G` equals the number of
subgroups of `G`. -/
theorem card_poissonSets_eq_card_subgroups :
    Nat.card {S : Finset G // S.Nonempty ∧ PoissonSet S} = Nat.card (AddSubgroup G) :=
  Nat.card_congr poissonSetEquivSubgroup

/-- The correspondence is an order isomorphism: for a nonempty Poisson set `T` and *any*
finset `S`, inclusion `S ⊆ T` is equivalent to the corresponding inclusion of generated
subgroups.  Applied to two Poisson sets this says that `poissonSetEquivSubgroup` preserves
and reflects the order. -/
theorem poissonSet_subset_iff_le {S T : Finset G} (hTne : T.Nonempty) (hT : PoissonSet T) :
    S ⊆ T ↔ closureS S ≤ closureS T := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    rw [closureS, AddSubgroup.closure_le]
    intro x hx
    have hxT : x ∈ T := h (by exact_mod_cast hx)
    exact AddSubgroup.subset_closure (by exact_mod_cast hxT)
  · intro h x hx
    have hxS : x ∈ closureS S := AddSubgroup.subset_closure (by exact_mod_cast hx)
    have hxT : x ∈ closureS T := h hxS
    have hTeq := subgroup_of_poissonSet hTne hT
    rw [hTeq]
    exact mem_closureF.2 hxT

/-- Poisson sets are closed under intersection. -/
theorem poissonSet_inter {S T : Finset G} (hS : PoissonSet S) (hT : PoissonSet T)
    (hST : (S ∩ T).Nonempty) : PoissonSet (S ∩ T) := by
  rw [poissonSet_iff_comb] at hS hT ⊢
  refine Or.inr ⟨?_, ?_⟩
  · obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := hST
    rcases hS with rfl | ⟨h0S, _⟩
    · exact absurd (Finset.mem_inter.1 hz).1 (by simp)
    rcases hT with rfl | ⟨h0T, _⟩
    · exact absurd (Finset.mem_inter.1 hz).2 (by simp)
    exact Finset.mem_inter.2 ⟨h0S, h0T⟩
  · intro x hx y hy
    obtain ⟨hxS, hxT⟩ := Finset.mem_inter.1 hx
    obtain ⟨hyS, hyT⟩ := Finset.mem_inter.1 hy
    rcases hS with rfl | ⟨-, hsubS⟩
    · exact absurd hxS (by simp)
    rcases hT with rfl | ⟨-, hsubT⟩
    · exact absurd hxT (by simp)
    exact Finset.mem_inter.2 ⟨hsubS x hxS y hyS, hsubT x hxT y hyT⟩

set_option maxRecDepth 40000 in
/-- Poisson sets are **not** closed under union: in the Klein four-group the union of the two
Poisson sets `{0,(1,0)}` and `{0,(0,1)}` is not Poisson.  So the Poisson spectrum is a
meet-semilattice inside the Boolean algebra of subsets, but not a sublattice. -/
theorem not_poissonSet_union_example :
    PoissonSet ({0, (1, 0)} : Finset (ZMod 2 × ZMod 2)) ∧
    PoissonSet ({0, (0, 1)} : Finset (ZMod 2 × ZMod 2)) ∧
    ¬ PoissonSet (({0, (1, 0)} : Finset (ZMod 2 × ZMod 2)) ∪ {0, (0, 1)}) := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [poissonSet_iff_comb]; exact Or.inr ⟨by decide, by decide⟩
  · rw [poissonSet_iff_comb]; exact Or.inr ⟨by decide, by decide⟩
  · rw [poissonSet_iff_comb]
    intro h
    rcases h with h | ⟨-, hsub⟩
    · revert h; decide
    · have := hsub (1, 0) (by decide) (0, 1) (by decide)
      revert this
      decide

end FourierFA


/- ===== Catalog/Pythagorean/FourierPoissonZMod.lean ===== -/

/-
# Exactly `d(n)` Poisson formulas on `ZMod n`

`Catalog.Pythagorean.FourierPoissonLattice` identifies the nonempty Poisson sets of a finite
abelian group with its subgroups.  For cyclic groups this turns the analytic question
"how many exact Poisson summation formulas does `ZMod n` support?" into a divisor count.

The subgroup count of a cyclic group is not available in Mathlib, so it is proved here:

* `FourierFA.addSubgroup_zmod_eq_of_card_eq` : a cyclic group has **at most one** subgroup of
  each order (proved through the bound `#{x : m • x = 0} ≤ m` valid in cyclic groups).
* `FourierFA.exists_addSubgroup_zmod_card_eq` : and at least one for each divisor, namely
  the subgroup generated by `n / d`.
* `FourierFA.subgroupZModEquivDivisors` : hence `AddSubgroup (ZMod n) ≃ n.divisors`.
* `FourierFA.card_addSubgroups_zmod` : `#AddSubgroup (ZMod n) = d(n)`.
* `FourierFA.card_poissonSets_zmod` : **the number of exact Poisson summation formulas on
  `ZMod n` is exactly the number of divisors of `n`** (OEIS A000005).

This generalises the exhaustively verified cases `n = 4, 5, 6, 8` of
`Catalog.Pythagorean.FourierPoissonCounting` to all `n`.
-/

import Mathlib
import Pythagorean.FourierPoissonLattice

open Finset Fintype
open scoped Classical

namespace FourierFA

variable (n : ℕ) [NeZero n]

/-- The carrier finset of a subgroup has the expected cardinality. -/
lemma card_subFinset_eq_card (H : AddSubgroup (ZMod n)) :
    (subFinset H).card = Nat.card H := by
  classical
  rw [Nat.card_eq_fintype_card, Fintype.card_subtype]
  rfl

omit [NeZero n] in
/-- Every element of a subgroup is killed by the subgroup order. -/
lemma nsmul_card_eq_zero_of_mem {H : AddSubgroup (ZMod n)} {x : ZMod n} (hx : x ∈ H) :
    (Nat.card H) • x = 0 := by
  have h : (Nat.card H) • (⟨x, hx⟩ : H) = 0 := card_nsmul_eq_zero'
  exact congrArg (Subtype.val) h

/-- **A cyclic group has at most one subgroup of each order.** -/
theorem addSubgroup_zmod_eq_of_card_eq (H K : AddSubgroup (ZMod n))
    (h : Nat.card H = Nat.card K) : H = K := by
  classical
  -- both carriers coincide with the `m`-torsion, where `m` is the common order
  have key : ∀ L : AddSubgroup (ZMod n),
      subFinset L = Finset.univ.filter (fun x : ZMod n => (Nat.card L) • x = 0) := by
    intro L
    have hpos : 0 < Nat.card L := Nat.card_pos
    have hsub : subFinset L ⊆ Finset.univ.filter (fun x : ZMod n => (Nat.card L) • x = 0) := by
      intro x hx
      exact Finset.mem_filter.2 ⟨Finset.mem_univ _,
        nsmul_card_eq_zero_of_mem n (mem_subFinset.1 hx)⟩
    have hcard : (Finset.univ.filter (fun x : ZMod n => (Nat.card L) • x = 0)).card
        ≤ (subFinset L).card := by
      rw [card_subFinset_eq_card]
      exact IsAddCyclic.card_nsmul_eq_zero_le hpos
    exact Finset.eq_of_subset_of_card_le hsub hcard
  have hHK : subFinset H = subFinset K := by rw [key H, key K, h]
  ext x
  have := congrArg (fun (s : Finset (ZMod n)) => x ∈ s) hHK
  simpa [mem_subFinset] using this

/-- The order of a subgroup of `ZMod n` is a divisor of `n`. -/
lemma card_addSubgroup_mem_divisors (H : AddSubgroup (ZMod n)) : Nat.card H ∈ n.divisors := by
  have hdvd : Nat.card H ∣ Nat.card (ZMod n) := AddSubgroup.card_addSubgroup_dvd_card H
  have hn : Nat.card (ZMod n) = n := by simp
  rw [hn] at hdvd
  exact Nat.mem_divisors.2 ⟨hdvd, NeZero.ne n⟩

omit [NeZero n] in
/-- **Existence**: every divisor of `n` is the order of a subgroup of `ZMod n`. -/
theorem exists_addSubgroup_zmod_card_eq {d : ℕ} (hd : d ∈ n.divisors) :
    ∃ H : AddSubgroup (ZMod n), Nat.card H = d := by
  obtain ⟨hdvd, hn0⟩ := Nat.mem_divisors.1 hd
  refine ⟨AddSubgroup.zmultiples (((n / d : ℕ) : ZMod n)), ?_⟩
  rw [Nat.card_zmultiples, ZMod.addOrderOf_coe _ hn0]
  have hdvd' : (n / d) ∣ n := Nat.div_dvd_of_dvd hdvd
  rw [Nat.gcd_eq_right hdvd']
  exact Nat.div_div_self hdvd hn0

/-- **The subgroups of `ZMod n` are indexed by the divisors of `n`.** -/
noncomputable def subgroupZModEquivDivisors :
    AddSubgroup (ZMod n) ≃ {d : ℕ // d ∈ n.divisors} :=
  Equiv.ofBijective (fun H => ⟨Nat.card H, card_addSubgroup_mem_divisors n H⟩)
    ⟨fun H K hHK => addSubgroup_zmod_eq_of_card_eq n H K (by simpa using congrArg Subtype.val hHK),
      by
        rintro ⟨d, hd⟩
        obtain ⟨H, hH⟩ := exists_addSubgroup_zmod_card_eq n hd
        exact ⟨H, Subtype.ext hH⟩⟩

/-- The number of subgroups of `ZMod n` is the number of divisors of `n`. -/
theorem card_addSubgroups_zmod :
    Nat.card (AddSubgroup (ZMod n)) = (Nat.divisors n).card := by
  rw [Nat.card_congr (subgroupZModEquivDivisors n), Nat.card_eq_fintype_card]
  exact Fintype.card_coe _

/-- **The number of exact Poisson summation formulas on `ZMod n` equals `d(n)`.**
Combining the classification of Poisson sets with the subgroup count of a cyclic group. -/
theorem card_poissonSets_zmod :
    Nat.card {S : Finset (ZMod n) // S.Nonempty ∧ PoissonSet S} = (Nat.divisors n).card :=
  (card_poissonSets_eq_card_subgroups).trans (card_addSubgroups_zmod n)

/-- A sample instance beyond the exhaustively checked range: `ZMod 12` supports exactly six
exact Poisson summation formulas, one for each divisor of `12`. -/
theorem card_poissonSets_zmod_twelve :
    Nat.card {S : Finset (ZMod 12) // S.Nonempty ∧ PoissonSet S} = 6 := by
  rw [card_poissonSets_zmod]
  decide

end FourierFA


/- ===== Catalog/Pythagorean/FourierPoissonSquares.lean ===== -/

/-
# Quadratic residue sets are never Poisson (except trivially)

The residue sets that govern the classical theory of Pythagorean triples — the squares
modulo `n` — are the natural test case for the converse of Poisson summation proved in
`Catalog.Pythagorean.FourierPoissonConverse`.  They are almost never subgroups, so by the
classification they never satisfy an exact Poisson summation formula, and the gap theorem
turns this qualitative failure into an explicit numerical lower bound.

Main results:

* `FourierFA.squaresF` : the set of squares in `ZMod n`.
* `FourierFA.poissonSet_squaresF_two`, `FourierFA.not_poissonSet_squaresF_three` …
  `FourierFA.not_poissonSet_squaresF_eight` : the squares mod `n` form a Poisson set for
  `n = 1, 2` and fail to for `3 ≤ n ≤ 8`.
* `FourierFA.closureF_squares_zmod8` : the squares mod `8` generate all of `ZMod 8`.
* `FourierFA.poisson_gap_squares_zmod8` : a **quantitative** failure — some Dirac delta
  supported on the squares mod `8` has Poisson defect of modulus at least `5`.  So the error
  in any attempted Poisson-type formula over the quadratic residues mod `8` is of the same
  order as the group itself, not a small perturbation.
-/

import Mathlib
import Pythagorean.FourierPoissonLattice

open Finset Fintype ComplexConjugate
open scoped Classical

namespace FourierFA

/-- The set of squares in `ZMod n`. -/
def squaresF (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] : Finset (ZMod n) := Finset.univ.image (fun a => a ^ 2)

/-- Modulo `2` every residue is a square, so the squares form a (trivial) Poisson set. -/
theorem poissonSet_squaresF_two : PoissonSet (squaresF 2) := by
  rw [poissonSet_iff_comb]
  refine Or.inr ⟨by decide, by decide⟩

theorem poissonSet_squaresF_one : PoissonSet (squaresF 1) := by
  rw [poissonSet_iff_comb]
  refine Or.inr ⟨by decide, by decide⟩

theorem not_poissonSet_squaresF_three : ¬ PoissonSet (squaresF 3) := by
  rw [poissonSet_iff_comb]
  intro h
  rcases h with h | ⟨-, hsub⟩
  · revert h; decide
  · have := hsub 0 (by decide) 1 (by decide)
    revert this; decide

theorem not_poissonSet_squaresF_four : ¬ PoissonSet (squaresF 4) := by
  rw [poissonSet_iff_comb]
  intro h
  rcases h with h | ⟨-, hsub⟩
  · revert h; decide
  · have := hsub 0 (by decide) 1 (by decide)
    revert this; decide

theorem not_poissonSet_squaresF_five : ¬ PoissonSet (squaresF 5) := by
  rw [poissonSet_iff_comb]
  intro h
  rcases h with h | ⟨-, hsub⟩
  · revert h; decide
  · have := hsub 1 (by decide) 4 (by decide)
    revert this; decide

theorem not_poissonSet_squaresF_six : ¬ PoissonSet (squaresF 6) := by
  rw [poissonSet_iff_comb]
  intro h
  rcases h with h | ⟨-, hsub⟩
  · revert h; decide
  · have := hsub 3 (by decide) 4 (by decide)
    revert this; decide

theorem not_poissonSet_squaresF_seven : ¬ PoissonSet (squaresF 7) := by
  rw [poissonSet_iff_comb]
  intro h
  rcases h with h | ⟨-, hsub⟩
  · revert h; decide
  · have := hsub 1 (by decide) 2 (by decide)
    revert this; decide

theorem not_poissonSet_squaresF_eight : ¬ PoissonSet (squaresF 8) := by
  rw [poissonSet_iff_comb]
  intro h
  rcases h with h | ⟨-, hsub⟩
  · revert h; decide
  · have := hsub 1 (by decide) 4 (by decide)
    revert this; decide

/-! ## A quantitative failure for the squares mod `8` -/

/-- The squares mod `8` are `{0, 1, 4}`. -/
theorem squaresF_eight : squaresF 8 = ({0, 1, 4} : Finset (ZMod 8)) := by decide

/-- Since `1` is a square, the squares mod `8` generate the whole group. -/
theorem closureF_squares_zmod8 : closureF ({0, 1, 4} : Finset (ZMod 8)) = Finset.univ := by
  refine Finset.eq_univ_iff_forall.2 fun x => ?_
  have h1 : (1 : ZMod 8) ∈ closureS ({0, 1, 4} : Finset (ZMod 8)) :=
    AddSubgroup.subset_closure (by simp)
  have hx : x = (x.val : ℕ) • (1 : ZMod 8) := by
    rw [nsmul_eq_mul, mul_one, ZMod.natCast_val, ZMod.cast_id]
  rw [mem_closureF, hx]
  exact AddSubgroup.nsmul_mem _ h1 _

/-- **Quantitative failure of Poisson summation over the quadratic residues mod `8`.**
Some Dirac delta supported on `{0,1,4}` has Poisson defect of modulus at least `5 = 8 - 3`. -/
theorem poisson_gap_squares_zmod8 :
    ∃ y₀ ∈ ({0, 1, 4} : Finset (ZMod 8)),
      (5 : ℝ) ≤ ‖poissonDefect ({0, 1, 4} : Finset (ZMod 8)) (delta y₀)‖ := by
  have hne : ({0, 1, 4} : Finset (ZMod 8)) ≠ closureF ({0, 1, 4} : Finset (ZMod 8)) := by
    rw [closureF_squares_zmod8]
    decide
  obtain ⟨y, hy, hb⟩ := poisson_gap ⟨0, by decide⟩ hne
  refine ⟨y, hy, le_trans (le_of_eq ?_) hb⟩
  rw [closureF_squares_zmod8]
  have h8 : (Finset.univ : Finset (ZMod 8)).card = 8 := by decide
  have h3 : ({0, 1, 4} : Finset (ZMod 8)).card = 3 := by decide
  rw [h8, h3]
  norm_num

end FourierFA
